## Veterinary Clinical Trials Market Trends

The global veterinary clinical trials market size was valued at USD 4.9 billion in 2023 and is projected to grow from USD 6.3 billion in 2026 to USD 8.9 billion by 2030, at a CAGR of 8.9% from 2024 to 2030. The market in North America dominated with a revenue share of 33.7% in 2023. The market is primarily driven by advancements in veterinary medicine, the rising prevalence of chronic and infectious diseases in animals increased investment from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies in veterinary research, and increased availability of funding and grants from both public institutions and private organizations.

Image: مصطفى السيد: نتواصل مع وزارة الصحة لإقرار تطبيق علاج السرطان بالذهب على البشر الدكتور مصطفى السيد

(أ ش أ)

أكد العالم المصرى الدكتور مصطفى السيد أنه يتم حاليا التواصل مع وزارة الصحة بصفة مستمرة لعرض نتائج تجارب استخدام جزيئات الذهب النانومترية فى علاج السرطان والرد على كافة استفساراتها، والتأكد من أن تلك الجزيئات لا تؤثر سلبيا على خلايا الجسم السليمة، لإقرار تلك الطريقة والبدء فى تطبيقها على البشر.

جاء ذلك خلال المحاضرة التى ألقاها الدكتور السيد، اليوم الأحد، فى الصالون العلمى لأكاديمية البحث العلمى والتكنولوجيا لعرض أحدث تطورات أبحاثه فى علاج السرطان بجزيئات الذهب النانومترية، وبدء إجراء تجارب سريرية لهذا النوع من العلاج، بحضور عدد كبير من طلاب الكليات العلمية والصيادلة ونخبة من أساتذة الجامعات والمراكز البحثية.

وعرض العالم المصرى فكرة علاج السرطان بجزيئات الذهب النانومترية القائمة على حقن قطع الذهب الصغيرة (نانو) داخل الجسم لتمتص الضوء تحت الأحمر وتسخن الخلية السرطانية للقضاء عليها، موضحا أن التجارب أثبتت أنه عقب تسخين قطع ذهب ورفع درجة الحرارة حول الخلية يتم انصهار أو "تسييح" الخلايا السرطانية والبروتينات حولها مما يمنع انتشارها فى باقى أجزاء الجسم، مؤكدا أن التجارب مستمرة لمعرفة طريقة تغير عمل الخلية السرطانية بعد اعتيادها على تلك الطريقة.

## Abstract

### Background

Feline plasma cell-derived neoplasms, including extramedullary plasmacytoma and multiple myeloma, are rare and frequently associated with poor prognosis. Bortezomib, a proteasome inhibitor used to treat human multiple myeloma, has shown antitumor activity in canine and feline neoplastic cells. However, the clinical data on cats remain limited. This study retrospectively evaluated the clinical outcomes of cats with plasma cell-derived neoplasia treated with bortezomib, and explored the potential association between treatment response and endoplasmic reticulum stress-related marker expression.

### Methods

Medical records from two referral centers were reviewed to identify cats diagnosed with plasma cell-derived neoplasms that received at least one dose of bortezomib between April 2022 and December 2025. Treatment response was assessed using the Veterinary Cooperative Oncology Group (VCOG) response evaluation criteria for solid tumors in dogs v1 and by measuring changes in M protein production. Adverse events were graded according to the VCOG Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v2. Immunohistochemistry for activating transcription factor 6 was performed in representative responder and non-responder cases, and nuclear diaminobenzidine intensity was semi-quantified using the QuPath software.

### Results

Five cats met the inclusion criteria. Objective responses were observed in four cases, including two cases each of complete and partial remission. The progression-free interval ranged from 10 to > 811 days. All responding patients exhibited M protein production, whereas non-responding patients did not. Bortezomib is generally well tolerated, with transient neutropenia and peripheral neuropathy being the most notable adverse events reported. Semiquantitative analysis of immunostaining for activating transcription factor 6 demonstrated higher nuclear expression intensity in complete responders than in non-responders.

### Conclusions

This retrospective pilot case-series suggests that bortezomib exhibits therapeutic activity against feline plasma cell-derived neoplasms.

Title: Modeling the Microenvironmental Dynamics of Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma in Lacrimal Gland with Treatment Intervention
Authors: Ayasa Akter, Miss Sajnin Binta Salam Efty, Uzzwal Kumar Mallick
Date: Tue Oct 13 11:51:17 2026

Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the lacrimal gland is a rare and extremely life threatening malignant tumor with a high risk of recurrence and poor long-term outcomes. On the other hand, due to its complex molecular dynamics and low incidence rate, treatment strategies are very limited. In this study, a mathematical model is developed based on the biological phenomena of the tumor microenvironment using nonlinear ordinary differential equations. It is analyzed both analytically and numerically. According to the findings, the growth of tumor cells is associated with the depletion of oxygen and nutrients, while severe hypoxia promotes the development of abnormal blood vessels and makes tumor control more difficult. Surgery and postoperative radiotherapy have been considered as treatment strategies, and we have observed that surgery alone may not be sufficient to prevent the regrowth of residual tumor cells. In addition, postoperative radiotherapy provides better control of the residual tumor burden, particularly when the remaining tumor cells have higher radiosensitivity. Furthermore, different radiotherapy interruption scenarios have been investigated, and the results indicate that longer gaps between radiotherapy doses can adversely affect the overall treatment response, leading to increased overall toxicity and a higher number of residual tumor cells at the end of the observation period. Consequently, our results suggest that postoperative radiotherapy after surgery, combined with adequate radiosensitivity of the residual tumor cells and adherence to the prescribed treatment schedule without prolonged interruptions, may reduce the risk of tumor recurrence and potentially improve long term survival.

Title: Can $^{225}$Ac be imaged on a long axial field-of-view PET/CT with standard clinical settings?
Authors: Lorenzo Mercolli
Date: Tue Oct 13 19:42:22 2026

Purpose: The $^{225}$Ac decay chain includes $^{209}$Tl, whose prominent 1567 keV gamma line can create electron-positron pairs. We investigated whether a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET/CT can image $^{225}$Ac using standard clinical acquisition and reconstruction methods. Methods: A syringe placed next to a vial (5.89 and 10.29 MBq of $^{225}$Ac activity) and a NEMA IEC body phantom (sphere activity concentration 4.56 kBq mL$^{-1}$) were scanned for 45 and 60 min, respectively, on a Biograph Vision Quadra (Siemens Healthineers). To support our findings, FLUKA simulations scored the annihilation locations around a $^{225}$Ac point source. Results: The contours of the syringe and vial were visible despite high noise, but the NEMA spheres could not be distinguished from the background. As illustrated by the FLUKA simulations, the number of annihilation events decreases exponentially according to the mean free path of the 1567 keV photon in the surrounding medium. Conclusion: A LAFOV PET/CT can detect positrons created by pair production of the main $^{209}$Tl gamma line. However, these positrons are created where the photons interact with the surrounding medium rather than at the location of the $^{209}$Tl decays, which rules out standard PET imaging of $^{225}$Ac.
